source_note: External-review iter-1 findings from GPT-5 Codex (cross-AI; fresh-context vs Claude Opus 4.7 which authored proposal artifacts AND internal review iter-1). 9 findings: 2 CRITICAL, 5 WARNING, 2 SUGGESTION.
pushback_verification: All 9 findings verified against current artifact state at walk-time. Notable pushback on EC1: external AI recommended /opsx:ff as the correct command name; verified via grep (5 hits across fast-forward.md / onboard.md / openspec-onboard SKILL.md) — external AI was correct AND my session-start available-skills indexer showed 'opsx:fast-forward' as a separate drift. Adopted external AI's /opsx:ff name. Zero stale findings — no resolutions suppressed via pushback.

resolutions.action: Replaced /opsx:ff-change → /opsx:ff (10 occurrences), ff-change-<TS>.json → ff-<TS>.json (2), bare `ff-change` → `ff` (5) across proposal/design/tasks/explore/2 specs (6 files). Preserved SKILL filename `openspec-ff-change/SKILL.md` (filesystem path unchanged). Post-replacement sweep confirmed zero residue + no corruption + validation passes.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: Authored using the SKILL name as command name (openspec-ff-change → /opsx:ff-change). Should have read the actual command file.

resolutions.action: Split Audit-drift standalone recommendations requirement into change-scoped vs project-wide sub-cases. Each has distinct emit path (openspec/changes/<name>/.orbit-runs/ vs openspec/.orbit-runs/), change field value (name vs null), and recommendation logic (defer-to-prior vs no-prior-to-defer-to). Added 2 new scenarios for project-wide case; kept existing scenarios for change-scoped.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: C4 fix earlier addressed audit-drift refinement but didn't carve out the project-wide variant the existing schema documents.

resolutions.action: User chose option A (operationalize — drop implicit continuation rule). Conversation-boundary signals collapsed from 3 to 2: rule 1 = explicit user stop/pause, rule 2 = AI-initiated wrap. Added canonical orbit UX convention (AI should include explicit wrap phrase on handoff) and known-limitation note (user-walks-away case loses timeline capture but on-disk artifacts survive). Updated 1 scenario + added 1 new scenario for the known limitation.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: My W3 fix introduced rule 1 with the implicit 'next user message does not continue' clause that required future knowledge — unimplementable at JSON-write time.

resolutions.action: orbit-conventions's editorial per-kind extension now marks findings_summary / finding_titles as 'included when findings are present' with explicit call-out that review-external T0 omits them. Split editorial-emit-shape scenario into with-findings vs pre-findings-T0 variants.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: C1's unification was too strict for the pre-findings T0 case — required fields that don't exist yet.

resolutions.action: design.md Non-Goal rewritten to draw the right line: capability-spec-level harmonization (out — only orbit-conventions gets a MODIFIED delta) vs SKILL.md-level behavior harmonization (in — task 1.4 adds kind to existing emits). Contradiction with task 1.4 resolved.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: S1 fix added task 1.4 (in-scope harmonization) without updating the stale non-goal entry that said harmonization was out-of-scope.

resolutions.action: Task 1.2 expanded to cover 4 schema reference files (added archive-summary-schema.md). Swept proposal.md (2 spots) and design.md (3 spots) updating '3 existing per-skill schema references' → '4', each mention now lists the archive ref explicitly.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: C3 + the design narrative cited '3 schema references' (the three named run-summary-schema.md files) and missed that openspec-archive-change has its own archive-summary-schema.md that needed parallel treatment.

resolutions.action: Verified via grep on opsx-status code: orbit-status DOES scan openspec/explore/ (enumerate_explorations() at line 231) but upstream openspec list does NOT (verified empirically — current openspec list output shows only openspec/changes/ entries). Updated crystallization warning consequence #3 to accurately reflect this distinction: 'visible to orbit-status' (kept) + explicit note that openspec list visibility comes only after /opsx:propose moves staging to openspec/changes/.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: Warning text drafted without verifying upstream CLI scan behavior; assumed openspec list would see explorations.

resolutions.action: Task 9.6 README link target updated from openspec/conventions/run-summary-emit-schema.md (path eliminated by C2) → openspec/specs/orbit-conventions/spec.md's Internal-run JSON summary format requirement + cross-reference to new orbit-run-summary-emit capability.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: C2's cleanup of openspec/conventions/ path references missed task 9.6 (sweep was scoped to group 1 tasks).

resolutions.action: Added explicit precedence rule to Verify fail-mode recommendations requirement: mode ③ > ① > ② > warn. Rationale: directs user to root cause first (fix spec → complete impl → resolve gaps). Added new scenario for overlapping fail signals.
resolutions.anchoring_root_cause: D13 / Verify fail-modes spec listed cases but didn't address precedence; my own implicit assumption was 'whichever fails first' but the spec didn't formalize it.

ripple_flagged_files_aggregate: (All ripple effects of the external findings were applied inline during this walk — proposal/design/tasks/explore + both spec files updated. No external ripples remain.)

post_resolution_state.scope_note: Delta count unchanged from prior iteration; external findings drove refinements (additions to existing requirements, scenario additions, text fixes) rather than structural additions/removals.
post_resolution_state.anchoring_audit: 8 of 9 findings traced to anchoring or incompleteness in prior in-context work: EC1 (anchored on SKILL name vs command name), EC2 (C4 missed project-wide variant), EW1 (W3 fix introduced unimplementable rule), EW2 (C1 unification too strict), EW3 (S1 fix contradicted stale non-goal), EW4 (C3 missed 4th schema ref), EW5 (warning text drafted without grep), ES1 (C2 cleanup missed task 9.6). 1 of 9 (ES2) is a true gap (precedence never specified, not an anchoring artifact). This pattern matches openspec-orbit#20's empirical evidence that external review catches what in-context anchoring suppresses.

final_assessment: All 9 external findings resolved. The external review validated the orbit-orbit-orbit dogfood discipline: GPT-5 Codex's fresh-context pass caught 8 substantive issues that in-context Claude Opus 4.7 (both author and internal reviewer) had anchored away from. Change validates with --strict; 14 deltas across 2 capabilities.
